title: Minimum Cost to Move Between Indices
summary: Given an increasing integer array nums, for each index x, find the closest adjacent index y with the minimum absolute difference.
statement: Given an increasing integer array nums, for each index x, find the closest adjacent index y with the minimum absolute difference. You can move to any adjacent index with the cost equal to the difference in their values, or to the closest index with a cost of 1. For each query [li, ri], calculate the minimum total cost to move from index li to index ri. Return an array of answers for each query.
constraints: nums is strictly increasing with at least two elements.
Move only between adjacent indices; the move costs one when the destination is a closest neighbor of the source, otherwise the value gap.
Return the minimum monotone-path cost for every [left,right] query.
reference_solution:
def minimum_index_move_cost(nums,queries):
    n=len(nums);forward=[0]*n;backward=[0]*n
    for i in range(1,n):
        gap=nums[i]-nums[i-1]
        forward[i]=forward[i-1]+(gap if i>1 and nums[i-1]-nums[i-2]<=gap else 1)
        backward[i]=backward[i-1]+(gap if i<n-1 and gap>nums[i+1]-nums[i] else 1)
    return [forward[right]-forward[left] if left<right else backward[left]-backward[right] for left,right in queries]

hints: On a line, any detour adds positive cost, so the optimal route follows adjacent indices monotonically.
Precompute the directed cost of every forward and backward edge using the closer-neighbor rule.
Prefix sums turn each monotone query into one subtraction.
The edge rule is local to its source; summing exactly those directed edges yields the unique no-detour path cost.
